title: An abelian variety spreads to an abelian scheme on a dense open
statement: Let $D$ be a Dedekind domain, $E=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$, and $A/E$ an abelian variety [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sc-abelian-variety]. There are a nonempty open subscheme $U\subseteq S$ containing its generic point and a smooth proper commutative $U$-group scheme $B$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism] with connected fibres, equipped with an isomorphism of $E$-group schemes $B_E\simeq A$ [def-pc-base-change]. Such a smooth proper group scheme with connected fibres is called an abelian scheme. Here a Dedekind domain means a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one. A group scheme over a scheme $T$ consists of multiplication, inverse and identity $T$-morphisms satisfying the group diagrams; it is commutative if multiplication is invariant under interchange of the two factors. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: BLR 1.4, paragraph before Theorem 3 and proof of Theorem 3 (printed pp.19-20, PDF pp.25-26); dense-open spreading of the abelian variety and its group structure; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; project literature copy WANTED

proof.text: Put $M=D\setminus\{0\}$. Index by the directed set $I$ of finite subsets $F\subseteq M$, ordered by inclusion, and put $d_F=\prod_{a\in F}a$ and $S_F=\operatorname{Spec}D[1/d_F]$. The empty product is $1$; $F\cup G$ is a common upper bound. These are affine principal opens of $S$, with affine transition maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-colimit-principal-localizations], $E=M^{-1}D$ is the colimit of the principal localizations. The finite-subset indexing gives the same colimit: a compatible family of maps from $D[1/d_F]$ is precisely a map from $D$ inverting every $a\in M$ (use $F=\{a\}$), so extends uniquely to $E$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] identifies $\operatorname{Spec}E$ with $\varprojlim_FS_F$. All stages are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Since no $d_F$ is zero, every $S_F$ contains the generic point $(0)$ of $S$.

By [def-sc-abelian-variety], $A\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is smooth and proper. Smoothness includes local finite presentation by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; properness includes quasi-compactness and separatedness by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A separated morphism is quasi-separated because its diagonal is a closed immersion, hence quasi-compact. Thus the finite-presentation convention of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] applies to $A$. Clause (1) of [thm-pd-spreading-out], applied to the system in step 1, gives a finitely presented $X_0\to S_{F_0}$ and an $E$-scheme isomorphism $\alpha:(X_0)_E\simeq A$. This is descent of the underlying scheme only; the operations are descended next.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, clause (1); BLR 1.4 p.19, limit-argument route

proof.text: The schemes $S_{F_0}$, $X_0$ and the finite powers $X_0^r$ over $S_{F_0}$, for $r\leq3$, are of finite presentation over $S_{F_0}$ and are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Indeed, product projections are base changes of $X_0\to S_{F_0}$, so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] applies; local finite presentation of their structural composites follows on affine charts from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. Iterating the source-permanence clause gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the powers. These statements persist at every later stage by the same base-change clause. Transport $m_A$, $i_A$, and $e_A$ through $\alpha$ to morphisms on $(X_0)_E$. Apply clause (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to the three pairs $(X_0^2,X_0)$, $(X_0,X_0)$ and $(S_{F_0},X_0)$. Taking a common later index gives $m:X_1^2\to X_1$, $i:X_1\to X_1$ and $e:S_{F_1}\to X_1$ with exactly those generic restrictions. Fibre products and their base-change identifications use their universal property; in particular $(X_1^r)_E$ is identified with $A^r$.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, clause (2); schemes.tex Tags 03GI, 01KU; morphisms.tex Tag 01TS

proof.text: Consider the following six pairs of parallel morphisms, all defined over $S_{F_1}$: $m\circ(m\times1)$ and $m\circ(1\times m)$ from $X_1^3$; $m\circ(e\circ p,1)$ and $1_{X_1}$ from $X_1$; $m\circ(1,e\circ p)$ and $1_{X_1}$ from $X_1$; $m\circ(i,1)$ and $e\circ p$ from $X_1$; $m\circ(1,i)$ and $e\circ p$ from $X_1$; and $m\circ\mathrm{swap}$ and $m$ from $X_1^2$, where $p:X_1\to S_{F_1}$. The first five equalities hold generically by the group identities on $A$, and the sixth by [lem-sc-av-commutative]. Clause (3) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] makes each equality hold at some later stage. Taking the union of the finitely many resulting indices makes all six hold simultaneously. Hence we obtain a commutative group scheme $X_2/S_{F_2}$ and a group isomorphism $(X_2)_E\simeq A$. Subsequent base change preserves these equalities, since it preserves composition and finite products.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, clause (3); groupoids.tex Tag 0BFD, lemma-abelian-variety-abelian

proof.text: By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], $A/E$ is geometrically integral and in particular geometrically connected. The base $S_{F_2}$ is irreducible, with generic point $(0)$ and residue field $E$, because $D[1/d_{F_2}]$ is a domain. The structural morphism of $X_2$ is of finite type since it is of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-geometrically-connected-spread] to obtain an open $W\subseteq S_{F_2}$ containing $(0)$ over which all fibres are geometrically connected. A principal-open basis neighbourhood of $(0)$ inside $W$ has the form $D(a)$ in $S_{F_2}$ for a nonzero $a\in D$ (clear a power of $d_{F_2}$ from its defining fraction). Replacing $F_2$ by $F_2\cup\{a\}$ restricts $X_2$ to that neighbourhood. All later stages are open restrictions of it, so their fibres, with their residue fields, are the same fibres as before and remain geometrically connected.

Use the cofinal tail of the system after step 5; its limit is still $\operatorname{Spec}E$ by the same localization calculation as step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-smooth-qcqs] to the structural morphism of this stage model. Its source and base are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, it is locally of finite presentation by step 3, and its limit is $A/E$, which is smooth. Thus there is a stage after which every later structural morphism is smooth. Start at such a stage and apply [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-proper]. Its source and base are again quasi-compact and quasi-separated, its structural morphism is locally of finite type, and its limit $A/E$ is proper. This gives a further stage $F$ at which the structural morphism is proper; it is also smooth by the previous eventual assertion. The commutative group identities and geometrically connected fibres from steps 4 and 5 still hold there.

source.place: Tags 0C0C, lemma-descend-smooth, and 081F, lemma-eventually-proper, in Situation 081D

proof.text: Take $U=S_F\subseteq S$ and $B=X_F$. Step 1 shows that $U$ contains $(0)$ and is nonempty. Step 6 gives smoothness and properness, and steps 4 and 5 give the commutative group structure and connected fibres. The original $\alpha$ still identifies $B_E$ with $A$, and the descended operations make it an $E$-group isomorphism. These are exactly the required data.
